title: What soul means and Smith's objection to 'soul music'
summary: Goodwin says soul is playing what you feel; Smith complains of audiences asking for soul music after a set full of it.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Sure, and I think this is the best thing for a fellow. You know, this brings us down to what we call soul. This is a guy playing what he feels. This is a person playing what he feels. This is where the word soul comes from because he is playing himself. He is playing what we call soul.

I'm glad you mentioned that Crook and I'll tell you why. You know, over the years we've been playing together, we've come off -- I would say that practically every number we play is soul. We play it really from the gut and it always infuriates me when I get off the stand and some guy says, 'Can you play any soul music', and we've just knocked ourself out with ten choruses of soul music.
What, I wonder, do people mean by that term soul music when a jazz band is playing with its soul practically every number? This just infuriates me.

Well, I think the answer to that is you take a person that doesn't know music and they don't have music appreciation because they don't know one note from the other. Well they'll hear a word, they'll hear a term and they'll ask for something and if you play it for them, they don't know what it is, you understand what I'm saying?
But you'll take some guys, just like I'll revert back to where I was saying about these guys passing the music around for the guys because they thought you couldn't read, you know. It's just a thing.
